name: hayahash
workload: wasm32 build (Zig 0.16, -O3, no SIMD/wide-multiply) hashing 8-byte chained calls and 1 MiB bulk data under Node.js 26 / V8 on an Apple M1 Pro, comparing hayahash64/128 against ChibiHash v2, XXH3-64, XXH64, and rapidhash v3
claimed_speedup: hayahash64 reaches 23.55 GB/s bulk (1 MiB) vs XXH3-64's 17.41 GB/s and XXH64's 14.71 GB/s in the wasm32 baseline; hayahash128 hits 23.34 GB/s, also beating both. XXH64 still wins 8-byte chained latency (5.9 ns vs hayahash64's 7.7 ns).
compiler_and_flags: Zig 0.16 -O3 targeting wasm32 (no SIMD/wide-multiply instructions); competitor sources fetched at pinned upstream revisions
hardware: Apple M1 Pro; wasm32 module run under Node.js 26 / V8
tradeoffs: Author explicitly states there is no current native (non-wasm) competitive claim vs wyhash/rapidhash/komihash/gxhash/mx3 since the digest last changed; the wasm baseline must emulate wide multiplication for rapidhash, which may unfairly penalize it relative to native builds.
caveats: The win over XXH3-64/XXH64 is scoped to a wasm32, no-SIMD/no-wide-multiply environment; native x86/ARM rankings are not claimed to be the same. Brand-new repo with negligible external usage so far.
found_via: GitHub: gh search repos "non-cryptographic hash function" --sort stars, then gh api repos/thevilledev/hayahash/contents/docs/benchmarks.md

name: haya32x64
workload: Pure-JavaScript and wasm one-shot hashing of a 4-byte key and 1 MiB bulk data on AWS EC2 C8a (AMD EPYC 9R45) and C8g (Arm Neoverse V2), Node.js 24.18 / V8 13.6, medians of nine warmed public-API samples, comparing haya32x64 (32-bit-only state/arithmetic) against hayahash64, xxhash-wasm's XXH64, and cyrb53
claimed_speedup: haya32x64 pure-JS hashes a 4-byte key in 22.9 ns (C8a) / 34.0 ns (C8g) vs xxhash-wasm XXH64's 39.4 ns / 63.9 ns (~1.7x-1.9x faster short-key latency). XXH64 still leads 1 MiB bulk throughput: 15,973 MB/s vs haya32x64's 4,462 MB/s pure-JS (10,971 MB/s hybrid mode).
compiler_and_flags: Node.js 24.18 / V8 13.6 for JS/wasm figures; native SMHasher3 comparison built with GCC 15.2 -O3 -march=native
hardware: AWS EC2 C8a (AMD EPYC 9R45) and C8g (Arm Neoverse V2)
tradeoffs: Restricted to 32-bit state/arithmetic to target pure JS, CSP-restricted/edge runtimes, Cortex-M, RV32 and GLSL; loses on bulk throughput to 64-bit-multiply hashes like XXH64; digest is still labeled experimental and frozen at an interim verification value.
caveats: The speed win is specific to short-key hashing in pure-JS/32-bit-only environments; XXH64 (itself run via a wasm build) wins 1 MiB bulk throughput outright. Zero-star, ~7-week-old project from the same solo author as hayahash.
found_via: GitHub: gh search repos --topic non-cryptographic-hash --sort stars

name: HalftimeHash
workload: Hashing long strings (256KiB and 250KB) on an Intel i7-7800X (Skylake-X, AVX-512) and an AMD EC2 c5a.large (7R32, no AVX-512), comparing HalftimeHash variants against every hash family in the SMHasher suite (xxh128 included) plus clhash and UMASH for long-string almost-universal hashing
claimed_speedup: Paper text states the two fastest HalftimeHash variants are faster than every SMHasher-suite hash family, including xxh128, on 256KiB strings on the i7-7800X, and that HalftimeHash24 beats clhash/UMASH by up to 2x on strings up to 250KB on both the Intel and AMD chips. No exact HalftimeHash-vs-xxh128 numeric ratio appears in the paper's prose; the comparison is shown only in image figures (Figs. 5-7), so no invented ratio is reported here.
compiler_and_flags: Clang++ 11.0.1 on Ubuntu 18.04 (default build); reproducible via benchmark.cpp / cloud-benchmark.sh in the repo
hardware: Intel i7-7800X (Skylake-X, AVX-512); AMD EC2 c5a.large (7R32, no AVX-512)
tradeoffs: Header-only C++ almost-universal (AU) hash aimed at long-string hashing; wins shown are for 250-256KiB-class strings, not short-key hash-table lookups where xxHash/wyhash are typically used; AU construction needs larger per-instance keyed parameters than a plain xxHash seed.
caveats: Numeric speed ratios versus xxh128 live only in paper figures (images), not machine-readable text or a committed results table, so the entry cites the qualitative claim only. Repo last committed over a year ago (stale) and has few stars.
found_via: GitHub: gh api repos/jbapple/HalftimeHash (candidate check after seed query "hash function faster than xxHash wyhash benchmark"), then gh api .../contents/halftime-hash.tex
